Locate a defect in images (experimental)

Source: R/locate.R
locate.Rd

locate() asks TypeSafe where the defect is in each image: a Choice over 9 tiles of the image with reference crops, then a Box in the two most likely tiles. These are the steps that passed the Box test of the study. On the 46 textile inputs of the package, one run of locate() pointed to 14 of the 14 local defects and put a box on 1 of the 23 nominal images (vignette("images"), section "Defect location").

Usage

locate(decider, image, defect, references, max_active = 10, rpm = NULL)

Arguments

decider

A decider from decider_typesafe() with Jev 1.14 or later, for example decider_typesafe("jev-1.14.0") or "jev-latest".

image

The images: paths, URLs or magick images, as in decide().

defect

One phrase for the defect, with its article, for example "a textile flaw (a small patch where the weave is replaced by noise)".

references

A list with nominal and defective. Each holds one or more images, as image does (paths, URLs or magick images): parts with no defect, and parts with the defect, at about the scale of a tile (half the side of an inspected image). locate() does not crop them.

max_active

The largest number of requests in progress at the same time. The default is 10.

rpm

The largest number of requests per minute, or NULL (the default) for no limit. The requests then go out evenly, one each 60 / rpm seconds.

Value

A tibble with one row for each image, in the input order:

.pred_defect

1 minus the probability of "none" in step 1.

.box_left, .box_top, .box_right, .box_bottom

The box as fractions of the width and the height of the image, with the origin at the top left. NA when step 1 says "none", and for a row with an error.

.box_confidence

The confidence that TypeSafe gives for the box, from 0 to 1. In the run of vignette("images"), the two boxes that were not on a local flaw had 0.03 and 0.06, and the 14 boxes on a local flaw had 0.64 to 0.92.

.wording

The wording of the box: "generic" ("the defect") or "defect" (the phrase of defect).

.input_tokens

The input tokens of the requests of the image.

.cost

NA: TypeSafe does not report a cost.

.seconds

The time of the requests of the image.

.error

NA, or why the row has no answer. The text starts with the step: "Step 1" or "Step 2". After an error in step 2, the row keeps .pred_defect of step 1.

The attribute requests is the number of requests sent: one or two for each image.

Details

Box is experimental. Only Jev 1.14 and later have it, and TypeSafe can change it between releases. Check the boxes on images with a known defect before you use them.

Steps

  1. One request for each image: a Choice "Which picture shows defect? Compare it with the examples." over 9 tiles of half the image, with 50% overlap, and the answer "none". The tiles and the references are sent at 560 pixels. The references go in the state, with a note that names each of them.

  2. If the answer is not "none", one more request: a Box in each of the two most likely tiles (grown by 1.2, sent at 1024 pixels), with two wordings: "the defect", and defect with its first article changed to "the". The answer is the box in the most likely tile, with the wording whose two boxes agree more; on a tie, the wording with the higher mean confidence.

Each image is enlarged so that its short side is at least 280 pixels, the smallest size that TypeSafe takes. TypeSafe takes sides of 280 to 1568 pixels, so the long side of an inspected image can be at most 9 times its short side, and that of a reference 5.6 times. locate() stops before any request for a longer image.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dir <- system.file("extdata", "textiles", package = "decisions")
read <- \(f) magick::image_read(file.path(dir, f))
references <- list(
  nominal = list(
    magick::image_crop(read("nominal_textile_0630.jpg"), "125x125+62+62"),
    magick::image_crop(read("nominal_textile_0731.jpg"), "125x125+62+62")
  ),
  defective = list(
    magick::image_crop(read("local_textile_0199.jpg"), "125x125+56+68")
  )
)
locate(
  decider_typesafe("jev-1.14.0"),
  image = file.path(dir, "local_textile_0319.jpg"),
  defect = paste(
    "a textile flaw (a small patch where the regular diagonal weave is",
    "replaced by fine speckled noise)"
  ),
  references = references
)
} # }
